brief: The note argues US housing is not crashing but calcifying: record-age, high-equity, fixed low-rate homeowners have near-zero incentive to sell, so transaction volume has permanently broken lower rather than paused. That structural lock-in hurts brokerages, title companies and mortgage originators (a call to avoid them) while forcing renovation spending on aging housing stock (a call to go long repair/remodel names). Separately, affordability has narrowed the buyer pool to roughly the wealthiest 25% of households, so the note argues prices hold because demand is now wealth-driven rather than income-driven, favoring land developers/builders with premium-market lot inventories. Single-family and multifamily diverge: single-family delinquencies stay low, but multifamily delinquencies, negative rent growth and elevated vacancies/completions signal a rental "distress cycle," prompting an underweight call on affordable multifamily. A closing framework argues transaction-linked names are already repriced lower while renovation names (HD/LOW) have lagged and are underappreciated, a gap the note expects to widen if turnover stays frozen while remodeling spending holds.
